finding.claim: Pool.escape() builds SQL literals with backslash escaping whenever the pool has no connection to read status from. If the server runs with NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES, a quote escaped as \' does not escape it, so the literal can be broken out of. Impact is limited to callers that splice pool.escape() output into SQL text. It also needs a pool with no idle or active connections and a server in that sql_mode.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled string passed by application code to pool.escape(value) (pool.js:677-678), e.g. a username containing a quote
finding.sink: Escaped string concatenated into an SQL statement by the application and executed on a NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES server

trace.note: _searchInfo returns null when there is no idle or active connection
info == null yields noBackslashEscapes=false, so the backslash regex and map are used
A quote becomes \', which a NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES server reads as a backslash followed by a closing quote

finding.guards_checked: The null-info comment at utils.js:254 shows the fallback is intentional. Per-connection escape and parameterised queries use the live info.status, so they are not affected. The normal query path (packet-output-stream.js:382-393, 551-553, 639) checks STATUS_NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES. This candidate was not reproduced against a live server.
